jobs.title: Director, Technology Delivery
jobs.description:
Permanent Full Time

We are looking for a Director, Technology Delivery – Finance & Actuarial
to lead technology delivery across our Finance and Actuarial portfolio.

This is a leadership role spanning technology strategy, portfolio delivery, modernisation, operations and people. The Director will partner with business and technology leaders to shape multi-year technology roadmaps, deliver complex change and ensure the portfolio remains secure, resilient and positioned to support evolving business priorities.

The successful candidate will bring strong technology leadership, strategic thinking and delivery experience, with the ability to connect business priorities, technology direction and execution. They will operate effectively at both the strategic and delivery levels, build strong teams and partnerships, and bring clarity and accountability to a complex portfolio.

What you will do:

Lead technology delivery across the Finance and Actuarial portfolio, ensuring investment and delivery align with business priorities and strategic outcomes.
Partner with Finance and Actuarial leaders to translate business strategy into multi-year technology roadmaps, investment priorities and executable plans.
Help shape and execute the technology strategy for the portfolio, aligned with enterprise architecture and broader technology priorities.
Provide technology leadership across complex initiatives, from strategy, architecture and solution design through implementation, transition and ongoing operations.
Lead cross-functional teams spanning architecture, engineering, data, integration, security, operations and programme delivery.
Provide clear leadership across scope, funding, sequencing, dependencies, technology risk and delivery trade-offs.
Drive portfolio modernisation, reducing legacy complexity and technical debt while improving resilience, scalability and maintainability.
Ensure technology solutions are secure, sustainable and aligned with enterprise architecture, engineering, security and regulatory standards.
Build strong relationships across business and technology teams to manage dependencies and deliver integrated outcomes.
Lead strategic vendor and technology partner relationships, ensuring clear accountability for outcomes, quality, value and delivery commitments.
Drive portfolio planning and prioritisation, balancing transformation investment with modernisation, technical health, regulatory requirements and operational priorities.
Use portfolio, delivery and operational metrics to understand performance, identify opportunities and drive continuous improvement.
Build and develop high-performing teams, growing technical capability, developing future leaders and creating a culture of accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.
Provide senior leaders with clear visibility into portfolio health, investment requirements, key decisions, risks and outcomes.

What you will bring:

Post-secondary education in computer science, engineering, business or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Significant progressive experience in technology leadership and delivery, including leading and developing high-performing teams.
Demonstrated experience developing and executing technology strategies and multi-year roadmaps.
Strong delivery leadership, with the ability to translate business priorities into technology outcomes and drive complex initiatives through to delivery.
Experience leading complex initiatives across applications, data, integration, security and technology infrastructure.
Strong business, technical and architectural judgement, with the ability to balance strategic direction with pragmatic delivery decisions.
Demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships, influence across organisational boundaries and solve complex business problems through technology.
Experience with portfolio planning, investment prioritisation, financial management and vendor management.
Ability to navigate ambiguity, challenge existing approaches and make pragmatic decisions that balance business outcomes, risk, cost, quality and speed.
Strong communication and influencing skills, with the ability to make complex technology topics understandable to both technical and non-technical audiences.
A bias for action, curiosity and critical thinking, with the ability to adapt as business and technology priorities evolve.
A growth mindset and commitment to continuous learning and improvement.

What will set you apart:

Experience leading large-scale enterprise transformation programmes involving significant business, process and technology change.
Experience leading technology within Finance and/or Actuarial environments, or other complex financial-services functions.
Experience with ERP transformation or modernisation, with SAP S/4HANA experience considered a strong asset.
Experience working across global business segments and technology teams, navigating different priorities and operating models to deliver enterprise-wide outcomes.
Experience leading geographically distributed teams and working with global delivery models.
A track record of turning technology strategy and roadmaps into measurable business outcomes.

Permanent Full Time

Director, Network & Security AI and Automation

We are seeking a Director, Network & Security AI and Automation to establish and lead an engineering function within Network & Security Services with two complementary mandates: applying automation and AI to improve the engineering, delivery, and operations of network and security products; and building the security tooling, controls, and operational capabilities needed to protect AI platforms, applications, and agents. The Director will improve service speed, consistency, reliability, and scalability while helping Canada Life adopt AI securely and responsibly at scale.

Our ideal candidate combines strong network and security engineering experience with expertise in automation, AI-enabled operations, AI security, and technical leadership. You will establish reusable engineering patterns and use AIOps to strengthen operational visibility, proactive issue detection and response, and service resilience. Equally, you will lead the engineering and integration of capabilities that secure AI itself, protecting its supporting infrastructure, data access, integrations, and agent actions. Working with technology, security, and governance partners, you will translate AI security requirements into practical controls and sustainable services, with clear ownership and support models aligned to enterprise standards.

What you will do:

Establish and lead the Network & Security AI and Automation function, including its roadmap, delivery priorities, engineering standards, and long-term capability development across automation, AIOps, and security for AI.
Build and develop a team of technical practitioners, fostering software engineering discipline, continuous learning, collaboration, and accountability.
Partner with network and security product owners, engineering teams, and operations teams to identify and prioritize automation opportunities across the product and service lifecycle.
Deliver reusable automation for provisioning, configuration, testing, deployment, lifecycle management, and operational workflows across private and public cloud environments.
Establish Infrastructure as Code, API integration, orchestration, and DevSecOps practices, supported by version control, automated testing, controlled deployments, and reusable patterns.
Engineer AIOps capabilities that integrate telemetry and service context to improve observability, correlate events, detect anomalies, and support proactive issue detection and response.
Develop automated diagnostics and remediation with appropriate approvals, access controls, auditability, rollback, and human oversight to protect service resilience.
Lead the engineering and integration of AI security tooling and controls within the Network & Security Services mandate, partnering with enterprise architecture, information security, technology risk, identity, data, and AI platform teams.
Establish capabilities to discover AI services and agents, assess security posture, identify unmanaged AI use, and monitor access and activity across enterprise AI environments.
Engineer controls for AI platforms, applications, and agents, including secure connectivity, least-privilege access, data protection, policy enforcement, and restrictions on agent tools and actions, in partnership with accountable technology teams.
Define support models, documentation, runbooks, and operational readiness requirements with delivery and operations partners to sustain capabilities beyond initial implementation. Coordinate delivery across technology partners and vendors, aligning dependencies, platform integrations, and investment priorities with enterprise standards and roadmaps.
Manage the function’s resources and tooling investments, balancing innovation and delivery with security, maintainability, cost, and long-term supportability.

What you will bring:

Post-secondary degree or diploma in information technology, computer science, engineering, or an equivalent combination of training and experience.
Significant experience delivering and supporting highly available enterprise network and security platforms, with demonstrated leadership of engineering teams and cross-functional initiatives.
Proven ability to establish or mature an automation capability, translating business priorities into a practical roadmap, reusable solutions, and sustainable operating practices.
Strong foundational knowledge of enterprise networking, security products, and private and public cloud infrastructure, including their integration and operational requirements.
Practical experience with Infrastructure as Code and configuration automation tools such as Terraform and Ansible, scripting or development languages such as Python or PowerShell, and API-based integrations.
Strong understanding of software engineering and DevSecOps practices, including source control, CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, secrets management, secure deployment, and rollback.
Experience with observability platforms, telemetry integration, event correlation, and operational analytics, with the ability to apply AI and machine learning to appropriate operational use cases.
Strong understanding of security for generative AI platforms, applications, and agents, including risks involving prompt injection, sensitive data exposure, excessive permissions, and unauthorized tool use.
Experience engineering and integrating enterprise security controls, with the ability to apply secure connectivity, identity and access controls, data protection, security posture management, and monitoring to AI environments.
Ability to translate AI security and governance requirements into technical controls, reusable implementation patterns, and operational capabilities in collaboration with accountable enterprise partners.
Experience establishing production readiness, support ownership, documentation, and service management integration for engineering solutions.
Strong business acumen and the ability to prioritize investments, assess delivery trade-offs, manage vendor relationships, and demonstrate measurable value.
Proven ability to coach and develop technical practitioners and build effective relationships across engineering, operations, architecture, security, and risk teams.
Strong communication and influencing skills, with the ability to explain technical opportunities, dependencies, and risks to senior leaders and delivery partners.
Ability to adapt to an evolving technology landscape while maintaining disciplined engineering, secure implementation, and reliable service delivery.
Relevant professional certifications in cloud, networking, security, automation, or AI are an asset.
Experience in financial services or another regulated enterprise environment is an asset.

What if your next role gave you the opportunity not only to advance BIM practices, but to directly influence how a national engineering firm designs, collaborates, and delivers its projects?

BPA is looking for a Director, BIM to lead the evolution of our BIM practices and digital production tools across Canada.

jobs.description:
At Arctic Wolf, you won’t just watch the cybersecurity industry evolve – you'll help lead the change. Our global Pack is made up of people who thrive on solving hard problems, moving fast, and building technology that protects organizations around the world. We’re proud to be recognized by Forbes, CNBC, Fortune, CRN, Gartner Peer Insights and IDC MarketScape – but what matters most is the work behind it: delivering real outcomes for customers through award winning innovation like our Aurora Platform.

If you’re looking for meaningful work, smart teammates and the chance to make a real impact in a high-growth company that’s redefining security operations, Arctic Wolf is the right place for you!

Our mission is simple: End Cyber Risk. We’re looking for Senior Director, Product - Threat Intelligence & Detection
to be part of making this happen.   

LOCATION
: This role is open to Remote-United States, Remote-Canada, Hybrid-Eden Prairie-MN-USA, Hybrid-Waterloo-ON-CAN.

This senior product management lead role for Arctic Wolf defines and evangelizes the commercial strategy and product roadmap for threat intelligence & threat hunting along with delivering on the platform strategy to drive detection efficacy and efficiency for the latest threats keeping our customers safe. You will collaborate with Architecture, Engineering, Security Research, and cross-functional teams to align product vision with company goals, guide strategic planning, and drive innovation and outcomes in threat intelligence, threat hunting and detection engineering. You will lead initiatives to map strategy to execution, commission research, define OKRs, and maintain alignment across product lines and stakeholders. As a respected leader in the cybersecurity space, you will influence organizational structure, drive cross-team buy-in, mentor others, and represent your group with transparency and integrity.

Role Scope

Presents at stakeholder meetings to communicate the vision and alignment with corporate strategy
Works with product principals and engineering leaders to communicate strategy and high-level roadmap for threat intelligence, detections, and AI related initiatives to Leadership, PM and Engineering teams
Participates in cross-functional efforts and co-design to ensure product initiatives leverage existing security research capabilities and avoid redundant development
Decides (with Architecture and Security Research leadership) when new threat detection or intelligence capabilities are sufficiently differentiated to create new products or platforms and deliver highest value in efficacy and efficiency
Creates vision and strategy presentations and documents that address high-level cybersecurity problems, emerging threat landscapes, and AI-driven solutions
Defines and drives the strategic vision for threat intelligence and threat hunting while overseeing the incubation of breakthrough threat detection capabilities that improve effectiveness of our products (MDR, EDR) and the SOC
Leads cross-functional teams through product development, fostering a culture of experimentation, rapid iteration, threat validation, and customer-centric innovation in security
Partners with executive leadership to align threat intelligence and AI initiatives with long-term business goals, ensuring resource allocation and portfolio management driving high-impact security outcomes

Knowledge & Experience

Deep expertise in threat intelligence, threat hunting, detection engineering, and security research practices and their application to product development
Demonstrated understanding of conversational AI, large language models (LLMs), and machine learning applications in cybersecurity and threat intelligence and or detections is a plus
Collaborate and run cross-functional backlog reviews for threat intelligence and detections; participate in other product line reviews to contribute to overall organizational prioritization
Commission research into possible strategies to address customer security problems and evolving threat landscapes
Identify OKRs for threat intelligence, threat hunting and detections in support of wider corporate goals
Identify follow-up analysis and insights into emerging threat patterns and their implications for product strategy

Complexity and Problem Solving

Communicates to teams about process changes and the value these bring—provides clarity and answers questions about threat detection innovation priorities
Works with Engineering and Labs leadership to align threat intelligence, detection, and AI strategies with company direction, then breaks out specific initiatives to implement and support the strategy
Propagates priorities and "big rocks" to product principals and technical leaders to create an overall threat intelligence and detection product roadmap
Helps other product teams understand how threat intelligence, detections, and AI capabilities enable faster, more effective threat response in their solutions
Identifies projects that shift priorities and communicates with stakeholders across threat intelligence, security operations, and engineering teams

Collaboration & Interaction

Aligns cross-functional teams (Security Research, Engineering, Sales, Go-to-Market) on threat intelligence product strategies & roadmap to successfully meet the business needs
Drives buy-in and support from the SOC, security research, engineering, sales, and broader organization improving our threat intel and detection efficacy and efficiency
Creates documentation required for calibration efforts and prepares for reviews with evidence of achievements to represent the threat intelligence and detection portfolio

Required Qualifications

7+ years of progressive experience in cybersecurity, with deep expertise in threat intelligence, threat hunting, detection engineering, incident response, or security research—this is non-negotiable
10+ years of product management experience, including 3+ years at a director level or equivalent managing complex, cross-functional teams delivering enterprise security products at scale
Proven track record of taking products from strategy through successful market launch, with quantifiable results in revenue growth, customer adoption, or competitive market share expansion
Executive presence with ability to speak credibly to technical and non-technical audiences about cybersecurity strategy, emerging threats, and security innovation

Preferred Qualifications

Background in Threat Intelligence, managed security services (MSS), managed detection and response (MDR), or security operations centers (SOCs)
Experience within a fast-growth cybersecurity company or within a security labs/innovation division focused on emerging threats or technologies
Active presence and network within the cybersecurity community, threat intelligence organizations, security research ecosystem, or industry consortiums is a plus

What We're Looking For

A seasoned cybersecurity leader and product strategist who brings deep technical credibility and hands-on threat intelligence experience combined with strong executive product management acumen. You understand evolving threat landscapes and advanced adversary tactics, have direct experience with threat intelligence analysis and threat hunting, and are passionate about applying emerging AI technologies to revolutionize how organizations detect and respond to threats. You can operate effectively at the executive level, balance strategic vision with execution discipline, and drive organizational alignment on complex, multi-year threat defense initiatives. You thrive in a fast-paced, innovation-focused environment and have the credibility to influence executive decision-making on security investments.

About Arctic Wolf

At Arctic Wolf, we foster a collaborative and inclusive work environment that thrives on diversity of thought, background, and culture. Arctic Wolf recognizes that success comes from delighting our customers, so we work together to ensure that happens every day. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.

The Opportunity

Head of Finance

Oakville, Ontario (on-site)
Full-time, permanent

About Gastronomous

We are building the “Kitchen of the Future” for quick-service restaurants. We design, engineer and manufacture AI-powered kitchen automation: ChronoGrill™, an autonomous open-flame grill; Ghost, automated beverage pouring; and Gastroverse, our IoT cloud platform that monitors every machine in the field.

How we work.

We are a no-nonsense team of passionate, execution-driven people. Our ability to deliver, not just dream, sets us apart: inside and outside the company, we do what we say we will do. Our people are trusted to act independently, make practical decisions and move fast. We build the future one deployment at a time.

How fast we are growing.

The last 12 to 16 months changed the shape of the company:

Purchase orders signed with major brands, moving us from pilots to rollout
A new office in La Mirada, California to support US deployments; most of our customers are in the US, across many states
Our own ERP, built in-house to run parts, BOMs, inventory, work orders and purchasing

The next 12 to 16 months are bigger: scale across North America, sign new major accounts, enter new markets, secure new financing, and build an organization that can grow quickly and efficiently. We are about 35 people, mostly technical, headquartered in Oakville, Ontario.

Why This Role

A seat at the executive table. You report to the CEO, work directly with our founders, and help set company direction, not just report on it.
In the boardroom. You attend our quarterly board meetings and present the numbers, the plan and the trade-offs to our directors and investors.
Champion our growth. Every new account, market and financing round runs through your numbers. You will see your work show up in deals signed and machines deployed.
Breadth few finance roles offer. Two countries and counting, manufacturing, equipment, service and software revenue, government funding and venture fundraising, all in one seat.
Build it from the ground up. Our finance function, pricing model, financial controls and new-market playbook are yours to design. There is no inherited bureaucracy to work around.
A path to CFO. This role is designed to grow into CFO after the Series A.
A team behind you. You start with a full-time bookkeeper and build the team as the company grows.

What You Will Own

Your work falls into two halves of roughly equal weight. You run an efficient close, so you have real time for the decisions that grow the company.

Lead the finance function

You will set up our systems and processes and do much of the work yourself, making sure every entry, filing and payment is right.

Close and reporting. Lead the month-end close for our Canadian parent and US subsidiary, including consolidation and intercompany reconciliation. Deliver timely financial statements and management reports to leadership and the board.
Year-end. Lead year-end for both our Canadian and US entities: the year-end close, the audit or review engagement, and corporate tax returns, working with our external accountants.
Budget and forecasts. Own the annual budget and rolling forecasts, track performance against plan, and report the metrics leadership and the board run the company on: margins, unit economics and cash runway.
Revenue and billing. Own revenue recognition across equipment, service and software contracts. Set customer payment terms and manage deposits and milestone billing.
Accounts receivable. Own all of A/R across both entities: invoicing, customer credit and collections, so cash comes in on time.
Tax, audit and compliance. Manage Canadian and US compliance, including HST/GST, US sales tax, corporate filings and transfer pricing, working with our external advisors.
Payroll and benefits. Set up and run payroll in Canada and the US, including Records of Employment (ROEs). Administer our employee benefits programs, from enrolments and changes to provider relationships, keeping both accurate, compliant and cost-effective.
SR&ED and government funding. Assist with preparing our SR&ED claims, from tracking eligible costs to filing. Find, apply for, claim and report on grants and funding programs.
Systems and day-to-day accounting. Set up our accounting systems, internal controls and policies. Work hands-on with our bookkeeper on A/P, journal entries, reconciliations and expenses until each process runs cleanly.
Drive the financial side of our operations
Pricing and margins. Evaluate product and service pricing, build landed costing from bills of materials, contract-manufacturer quotes, freight and duties, and track margins.
Inventory and systems. Own inventory accounting and valuation, and keep our in-house ERP and QuickBooks reconciled so every cost and margin can be trusted.
US operations. Own the budget for our US office and work with its team to run it efficiently.
Cash and financing. Manage cash flow, working capital, banking relationships and USD/CAD exposure. Secure external financing, including inventory financing. Support equity fundraising: cap table, data room and financial diligence.
Business cases. Partner with operations, engineering and sales on capital purchases and investment decisions.
Insurance and risk. Manage our insurance program across Canada and the US, including renewals, coverage reviews and the certificates our customers require.
New markets. Build the financial setup for each new market we enter.

Who You Are

You are an operator, not a scorekeeper. Taking on new challenges that matter to the growth of a business is what excites you. You use the numbers to change a price, a budget or a contract. You find a way to deliver without a playbook, and you earn the trust of managers, suppliers, outside advisors and investors.

What You Bring

5+ years of progressive accounting and finance experience
You have owned finance end to end as the senior finance leader, or as the clear #2 who owned the close: monthly close, financial statements, and work with outside auditors and tax advisors
Hands-on: you have set up accounting systems and personally run payroll, A/R, A/P, journal entries and filings, not only reviewed them
A track record of owning finance-related operations beyond accounting, such as pricing, budgets or financing
Strong working knowledge of ASPE and/or IFRS
Advanced Excel and hands-on QuickBooks experience (QuickBooks Online preferred)
You can work on-site, 5 days/week at our Oakville headquarters

What Sets You Apart

CPA designation and a degree in accounting, finance or commerce
Manufacturing, hardware or equipment experience: inventory, standard or product costing, COGS, ERP
Experience in a fast-paced, growth-stage environment
Designing service, maintenance or recurring-revenue models for equipment
Government funding programs such as SR&ED and IRAP
Cross-border Canada/US finance: intercompany, USD/CAD, US GAAP, US sales tax and state filings
Leading people

What We Offer

A leadership role with a clear path to CFO

At Xe, we live currencies
. Founded in 1993, Xe is a global leader in currency exchange and international money transfers. Our Principles

At Xe, we value people who take initiative, think big, and follow through. We’re curious by nature and not afraid to ask what if or try something new. Everyone’s voice matters here. We expect people to speak up, bring ideas, and take ownership of their work. We don’t micromanage. We trust each other to make good calls, take responsibility, and move fast when it counts. And we care about community. Not in a vague corporate way, but in the sense that we have each other’s backs, stay open to feedback, and build a culture of trust and real collaboration.

Ambition. We dream big, try things out, and always ask “why not?” and “what if?” We’re ambitious in our thinking and our delivery.
Responsibility. We get involved, bring our perspective, and are always open to new ideas. We take personal responsibility.
Community. We value a sense of belonging, trusting each other, and encouraging authenticity. We contribute to our community.

The Role.
The Head of Consumer is the senior owner of Xe’s Consumer business in the United States and Canada, accountable for its strategy, proposition and commercial performance. Product, Marketing and Growth sit in global teams, so you will lead through influence: aligning them, along with Pricing, Sales, Customer Success, Care and Operations, behind the North America plan.

Responsibilities

This is a builder’s role. You will run the NAM Consumer business like a founder, owning revenue, profitability, acquisition, activation, retention, wallet share and customer lifetime value — and opening new channels to reach more customers. The role suits a digitally fluent leader with a background across product, marketing and growth in a fast-paced startup or scale-up. You know what great looks like in each function and can push global teams to deliver it for North American customers. Responsibilities include:

Consumer Strategy & Commercial Performance

Set and execute the North America Consumer strategy across the US and Canada, with clear plans to grow market share, revenue, customer value and profitability.
Own end-to-end commercial performance across the customer lifecycle: acquisition, activation, engagement, retention, wallet share and lifetime value.
Define the priorities, targets and operating rhythm for the Consumer business, and align regional and global stakeholders behind them.
Track a fast-moving competitive set — digital money transfer apps, neobanks, big tech wallets and incumbent banks — and spot new pockets of growth, such as high-value corridors and underserved diaspora communities.

Channel Expansion

Identify, build and scale new acquisition and distribution channels for Consumer in the US and Canada — for example, affiliate and referral programs, embedded and B2B2C distribution, community, diaspora and employer channels, and marketplaces.
Build the business case for each channel, run pilots, and scale those that hit CAC, volume and margin targets.
Lead commercial discussions with channel partners, including RFPs, and manage those relationships for ongoing performance.
Work with Compliance and Operations so each new channel launches safely and integrates cleanly into the customer journey.

Influencing Product, Marketing, Growth & Pricing

Be the voice of the NAM consumer with global Product, Marketing and Growth teams: bring market insight, set regional priorities, and secure roadmap and investment commitments.
Develop and own Customer Value Propositions for each Consumer segment in the US and Canada, and brief global teams on the features, benefits, pricing and service levels each segment needs.
Own regional go-to-market and in-market delivery of new products and propositions, coordinating cross-functional teams to maximize uptake and commercial return.
Champion test-and-learn on NAM funnels, onboarding and messaging, and hold partner teams to agreed outcomes.
Partner with Global Pricing on pricing and FX margin strategies that balance adoption, competitiveness, revenue, margin and retention.

Customer Experience & Service Delivery

Lead consumer service and sales performance across Customer Success and Digital Sales, ensuring service and sales SLAs are consistently met or beaten.
Partner with Care leadership so the global Care function serves NAM customers well, meets service levels and resolves complaints quickly.
Use customer feedback, app reviews, NPS, service data and root-cause analysis to remove friction across the journey.

Operational & Cross-Functional Leadership

Work with global Revenue Operations and Sales Operations to align regional strategy, global programs, annual targets and performance reporting.
Partner with North America Compliance leadership so the Consumer business meets its US and Canadian regulatory obligations — including state money transmitter licensing, CFPB remittance rules, FinCEN, FINTRAC and Bank of Canada requirements — while keeping the experience fast and customer-centric.
Build, lead and develop a high-performing team and create clear cross-functional accountability across regional and global stakeholders.

Performance Management & Reporting

Build and run a Consumer performance framework covering acquisition, conversion, activation, transactions, active customers, retention cohorts, revenue, profitability, CAC, LTV, channel performance, customer experience and product adoption.
Give senior leadership regular, insightful reporting that turns data into clear recommendations and actions.
Use data, customer insight and commercial analysis to guide investment decisions and close performance gaps.

How Success is Measured.
Success in the role will be measured through a combination of commercial, customer and operational outcomes, including:

Growth in Consumer revenue, margin and market share across the US and Canada.
Growth in active Consumer customers and transaction volumes.
Volume, revenue and unit economics from new channels launched and scaled.
Improved acquisition, conversion and activation, from sign-up to first transfer.
Increased retention, repeat usage and wallet share.
Adoption and commercial performance of new products and propositions in NAM.
Improved customer experience and service performance (e.g. NPS, app ratings, SLAs).
Stronger cross-functional execution and delivery of NAM priorities by global teams.

What You Bring

A digital-first operator who thinks in funnels, cohorts and experiments, and lives and breathes modern consumer apps.
Hands-on leadership experience across Product, Marketing and Growth — ideally having owned or run more than one of these functions.
A track record in a high-growth, fast-paced startup or scale-up environment, ideally in consumer fintech, payments, money transfer, neobanking or another digital consumer business.
Proven results scaling a consumer product: driving acquisition, activation, retention and monetization with measurable impact.
Fluency with the modern growth stack — product analytics, experimentation platforms, CRM and lifecycle tools, attribution and paid acquisition channels.
Strong commercial and analytical skills, with a firm grasp of unit economics (CAC, LTV, payback, contribution margin) and data-driven decision-making.
Experience building and leading high-performing, cross-functional teams, and comfort influencing in a matrixed global organization.
A bias for action: you move fast, ship, learn and iterate, while keeping the bigger strategic picture in view.
Excellent communication and storytelling, from team stand-ups to senior leadership.

You'll be part of a fast-moving team where your contributions directly impact growth. We invest in our people with tools, mentorship, and opportunities to level up fast-whether that's moving into closing roles or leadership paths. You'll also play a key role in shaping how we go to market in the competitive payments space, using real insights and industry benchmarks to stay ahead of the curve. The Opportunity

Gastronomous is hiring its first full-time Head of Finance, an executive role spanning finance and operations. You will sit at the executive table, report to the CEO, attend our quarterly board meetings, and build the financial backbone of a robotics company in the middle of a major scale-up.

This role keeps the books, and goes far beyond them. You will be a leader and a champion of our growth: shaping pricing, steering the finances of our operation, raising capital and helping take us into new countries. The role is built to grow into CFO after our Series A.

Head of Finance

Oakville, Ontario (on-site)
Full-time, permanent

About Gastronomous

We are building the “Kitchen of the Future” for quick-service restaurants. We design, engineer and manufacture AI-powered kitchen automation: ChronoGrill™, an autonomous open-flame grill; Ghost, automated beverage pouring; and Gastroverse, our IoT cloud platform that monitors every machine in the field.

How we work.

We are a no-nonsense team of passionate, execution-driven people. Our ability to deliver, not just dream, sets us apart: inside and outside the company, we do what we say we will do. Our people are trusted to act independently, make practical decisions and move fast. We build the future one deployment at a time.

How fast we are growing.

The last 12 to 16 months changed the shape of the company:

Purchase orders signed with major brands, moving us from pilots to rollout
A new office in La Mirada, California to support US deployments; most of our customers are in the US, across many states
Our own ERP, built in-house to run parts, BOMs, inventory, work orders and purchasing

The next 12 to 16 months are bigger: scale across North America, sign new major accounts, enter new markets, secure new financing, and build an organization that can grow quickly and efficiently. We are about 35 people, mostly technical, headquartered in Oakville, Ontario.

Why This Role

A seat at the executive table. You report to the CEO, work directly with our founders, and help set company direction, not just report on it.
In the boardroom. You attend our quarterly board meetings and present the numbers, the plan and the trade-offs to our directors and investors.
Champion our growth. Every new account, market and financing round runs through your numbers. You will see your work show up in deals signed and machines deployed.
Breadth few finance roles offer. Two countries and counting, manufacturing, equipment, service and software revenue, government funding and venture fundraising, all in one seat.
Build it from the ground up. Our finance function, pricing model, financial controls and new-market playbook are yours to design. There is no inherited bureaucracy to work around.
A path to CFO. This role is designed to grow into CFO after the Series A.
A team behind you. You start with a full-time bookkeeper and build the team as the company grows.

What You Will Own

Your work falls into two halves of roughly equal weight. You run an efficient close, so you have real time for the decisions that grow the company.

Lead the finance function

You will set up our systems and processes and do much of the work yourself, making sure every entry, filing and payment is right.

Close and reporting. Lead the month-end close for our Canadian parent and US subsidiary, including consolidation and intercompany reconciliation. Deliver timely financial statements and management reports to leadership and the board.
Year-end. Lead year-end for both our Canadian and US entities: the year-end close, the audit or review engagement, and corporate tax returns, working with our external accountants.
Budget and forecasts. Own the annual budget and rolling forecasts, track performance against plan, and report the metrics leadership and the board run the company on: margins, unit economics and cash runway.
Revenue and billing. Own revenue recognition across equipment, service and software contracts. Set customer payment terms and manage deposits and milestone billing.
Accounts receivable. Own all of A/R across both entities: invoicing, customer credit and collections, so cash comes in on time.
Tax, audit and compliance. Manage Canadian and US compliance, including HST/GST, US sales tax, corporate filings and transfer pricing, working with our external advisors.
Payroll and benefits. Set up and run payroll in Canada and the US, including Records of Employment (ROEs). Administer our employee benefits programs, from enrolments and changes to provider relationships, keeping both accurate, compliant and cost-effective.
SR&ED and government funding. Assist with preparing our SR&ED claims, from tracking eligible costs to filing. Find, apply for, claim and report on grants and funding programs.
Systems and day-to-day accounting. Set up our accounting systems, internal controls and policies. Work hands-on with our bookkeeper on A/P, journal entries, reconciliations and expenses until each process runs cleanly.
Drive the financial side of our operations
Pricing and margins. Evaluate product and service pricing, build landed costing from bills of materials, contract-manufacturer quotes, freight and duties, and track margins.
Inventory and systems. Own inventory accounting and valuation, and keep our in-house ERP and QuickBooks reconciled so every cost and margin can be trusted.
US operations. Own the budget for our US office and work with its team to run it efficiently.
Cash and financing. Manage cash flow, working capital, banking relationships and USD/CAD exposure. Secure external financing, including inventory financing. Support equity fundraising: cap table, data room and financial diligence.
Business cases. Partner with operations, engineering and sales on capital purchases and investment decisions.
Insurance and risk. Manage our insurance program across Canada and the US, including renewals, coverage reviews and the certificates our customers require.
New markets. Build the financial setup for each new market we enter.

Who You Are

You are an operator, not a scorekeeper. Taking on new challenges that matter to the growth of a business is what excites you. You use the numbers to change a price, a budget or a contract. You find a way to deliver without a playbook, and you earn the trust of managers, suppliers, outside advisors and investors.

What You Bring

5+ years of progressive accounting and finance experience
You have owned finance end to end as the senior finance leader, or as the clear #2 who owned the close: monthly close, financial statements, and work with outside auditors and tax advisors
Hands-on: you have set up accounting systems and personally run payroll, A/R, A/P, journal entries and filings, not only reviewed them
A track record of owning finance-related operations beyond accounting, such as pricing, budgets or financing
Strong working knowledge of ASPE and/or IFRS
Advanced Excel and hands-on QuickBooks experience (QuickBooks Online preferred)
You can work on-site, 5 days/week at our Oakville headquarters

What Sets You Apart

CPA designation and a degree in accounting, finance or commerce
Manufacturing, hardware or equipment experience: inventory, standard or product costing, COGS, ERP
Experience in a fast-paced, growth-stage environment
Designing service, maintenance or recurring-revenue models for equipment
Government funding programs such as SR&ED and IRAP
Cross-border Canada/US finance: intercompany, USD/CAD, US GAAP, US sales tax and state filings
Leading people

What We Offer

The chance to make your mark at a fast-paced company
A leadership role with a clear path to CFO
Stock options under our equity incentive plan
Health, dental and vision care
Disability, life and group insurance

At Xe, we value people who take initiative, think big, and follow through. We’re curious by nature and not afraid to ask what if or try something new. Everyone’s voice matters here. We expect people to speak up, bring ideas, and take ownership of their work. We don’t micromanage. We trust each other to make good calls, take responsibility, and move fast when it counts. Ambition. We dream big, try things out, and always ask “why not?” and “what if?” We’re ambitious in our thinking and our delivery.
Responsibility. We get involved, bring our perspective, and are always open to new ideas. We take personal responsibility.
Community. We value a sense of belonging, trusting each other, and encouraging authenticity. We contribute to our community.

The Role.

Product, Marketing and Growth sit in global teams, so you will lead through influence: aligning them, along with Pricing, Sales, Customer Success, Care and Operations, behind the North America plan.

Responsibilities

This is a builder’s role. You will run the NAM Consumer business like a founder, owning revenue, profitability, acquisition, activation, retention, wallet share and customer lifetime value — and opening new channels to reach more customers. The role suits a digitally fluent leader with a background across product, marketing and growth in a fast-paced startup or scale-up. You know what great looks like in each function and can push global teams to deliver it for North American customers. Responsibilities include:

Consumer Strategy & Commercial Performance

Set and execute the North America Consumer strategy across the US and Canada, with clear plans to grow market share, revenue, customer value and profitability.
Own end-to-end commercial performance across the customer lifecycle: acquisition, activation, engagement, retention, wallet share and lifetime value.
Define the priorities, targets and operating rhythm for the Consumer business, and align regional and global stakeholders behind them.
Track a fast-moving competitive set — digital money transfer apps, neobanks, big tech wallets and incumbent banks — and spot new pockets of growth, such as high-value corridors and underserved diaspora communities.

Channel Expansion

Identify, build and scale new acquisition and distribution channels for Consumer in the US and Canada — for example, affiliate and referral programs, embedded and B2B2C distribution, community, diaspora and employer channels, and marketplaces.
Build the business case for each channel, run pilots, and scale those that hit CAC, volume and margin targets.
Lead commercial discussions with channel partners, including RFPs, and manage those relationships for ongoing performance.
Work with Compliance and Operations so each new channel launches safely and integrates cleanly into the customer journey.

Influencing Product, Marketing, Growth & Pricing

Be the voice of the NAM consumer with global Product, Marketing and Growth teams: bring market insight, set regional priorities, and secure roadmap and investment commitments.
Develop and own Customer Value Propositions for each Consumer segment in the US and Canada, and brief global teams on the features, benefits, pricing and service levels each segment needs.
Own regional go-to-market and in-market delivery of new products and propositions, coordinating cross-functional teams to maximize uptake and commercial return.
Champion test-and-learn on NAM funnels, onboarding and messaging, and hold partner teams to agreed outcomes.
Partner with Global Pricing on pricing and FX margin strategies that balance adoption, competitiveness, revenue, margin and retention.

Customer Experience & Service Delivery

Lead consumer service and sales performance across Customer Success and Digital Sales, ensuring service and sales SLAs are consistently met or beaten.
Partner with Care leadership so the global Care function serves NAM customers well, meets service levels and resolves complaints quickly.
Use customer feedback, app reviews, NPS, service data and root-cause analysis to remove friction across the journey.

Operational & Cross-Functional Leadership

Work with global Revenue Operations and Sales Operations to align regional strategy, global programs, annual targets and performance reporting.
Partner with North America Compliance leadership so the Consumer business meets its US and Canadian regulatory obligations — including state money transmitter licensing, CFPB remittance rules, FinCEN, FINTRAC and Bank of Canada requirements — while keeping the experience fast and customer-centric.
Build, lead and develop a high-performing team and create clear cross-functional accountability across regional and global stakeholders.

Performance Management & Reporting

Give senior leadership regular, insightful reporting that turns data into clear recommendations and actions.

Growth in Consumer revenue, margin and market share across the US and Canada.
Growth in active Consumer customers and transaction volumes.
Volume, revenue and unit economics from new channels launched and scaled.

Increased retention, repeat usage and wallet share.
Adoption and commercial performance of new products and propositions in NAM.
Improved customer experience and service performance (e.g. NPS, app ratings, SLAs).

A digital-first operator who thinks in funnels, cohorts and experiments, and lives and breathes modern consumer apps.

A track record in a high-growth, fast-paced startup or scale-up environment, ideally in consumer fintech, payments, money transfer, neobanking or another digital consumer business.

Strong commercial and analytical skills, with a firm grasp of unit economics (CAC, LTV, payback, contribution margin) and data-driven decision-making.

About EQ3

EQ3 is a Canadian furniture company headquartered in Winnipeg, creating timeless furniture that brings together thoughtful design, quality materials and enduring value. Our business connects Canadian upholstery manufacturing, retail showrooms, e-commerce, and wholesale, giving our product development team a direct role in shaping our collections and the customer experience.

The opportunity

We are looking for a Director of Product Development to lead product strategy and development across the EQ3 portfolio. Reporting to the President, you will guide products from initial concept through development, launch and lifecycle management.

You will combine design judgment with commercial insight to build a cohesive assortment that delivers quality, comfort and value. Working closely with engineering, manufacturing, procurement, marketing, sales and operations, you will turn customer needs and business priorities into a clear product roadmap that supports profitable growth.

This position is based on-site in Winnipeg, Manitoba.

What You'll Do

Lead product strategy, planning and lifecycle management across the EQ3 portfolio.
Develop and manage the product roadmap, setting priorities, milestones and deliverables for new products and improvements to existing collections.
Translate customer feedback, market research and business insights into clear development briefs and business cases.
Guide decisions on materials, construction and product features, balancing design, quality, comfort, durability, cost and manufacturing feasibility.
Collaborate across departments to coordinate product launches and meet financial and customer satisfaction goals.
Evaluate assortment performance and identify opportunities to strengthen collections, improve margins, reduce unnecessary complexity and improve product availability.
Engage with customers and channel partners to understand product performance and emerging needs.
Present product direction, progress, business cases and risks to the President and other stakeholders.
Lead and develop the product development team, establishing clear expectations and strong working relationships across the business.

What You'll Bring

A master's degree in product leadership, business administration, marketing, finance, economics or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
A proven record of developing and launching successful products, managing product lines and building cohesive product portfolios.
Strong commercial judgment and the ability to translate customer research, market insights and performance data into practical decisions.
Demonstrated leadership skills and the ability to influence and align teams across functions.
Excellent communication, presentation and interpersonal skills.
Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
Experience in furniture, home furnishings or related consumer products is an asset, particularly in environments that connect design, materials and manufacturing.

Working at EQ3

Join a collaborative team where thoughtful design and practical problem-solving shape the work. You will have the opportunity to influence our product portfolio and work closely with colleagues across manufacturing and our customer-facing channels.

Community involvement, employee recognition and activities through the EQ3 Spirit Committee.
Opportunities for professional growth and internal advancement.
